text: Laid against the earlier promise, the difference grows smaller than at first it appears. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the narrator, having recalled this, turns that promise into a test. Much depends on a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel; and the word does not mean the same thing on any two of these occasions. Each time it costs Abraham more.
